title: Ergodic topology sampling toward the continuum with Stochastic Normalizing Flows
summary: In this work we provide numerical evidence that topological freezing in $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ Yang-Mills theory can be mitigated with a flow-based approach, as tested at lattice spacings as fine as 0.03~fm. We do so by analyzing the scaling of the costs of a computational strategy based on the combination of open boundary conditions and Stochastic Normalizing Flows. We show that the integrated autocorrelation time of the squared topological charge and the statistical uncertainty on the topological susceptibility remain under control throughout the explored parameter range with currently available computational resources. This marks an important step toward the use of even more efficient flow-based architectures for ergodic sampling of topology in state-of-the-art lattice gauge theory calculations.

AI.tldr: The study provides evidence that topological freezing in SU(3) Yang-Mills theory can be reduced using a flow-based method, showing controlled autocorrelation times and uncertainties, which is a significant step for efficient sampling in lattice gauge theory calculations.
AI.motivation: The motivation of this paper is to address the issue of topological freezing in SU(3) Yang-Mills theory, which hinders efficient sampling in lattice gauge theory simulations. The authors aim to demonstrate that a flow-based approach, specifically with Stochastic Normalizing Flows, can mitigate this problem, even at very fine lattice spacings.
AI.method: The method involves the use of open boundary conditions combined with Stochastic Normalizing Flows to analyze the scaling of computational costs. The researchers tested this approach at lattice spacings as fine as 0.03 fm, evaluating the integrated autocorrelation time of the squared topological charge and the statistical uncertainty on the topological susceptibility across a range of parameters.
AI.result: The results show that both the integrated autocorrelation time and the statistical uncertainty on the topological susceptibility are well-controlled over the explored parameter space, suggesting that the flow-based approach is effective in mitigating topological freezing with current computational resources.
AI.conclusion: The conclusion drawn from the work is that the use of Stochastic Normalizing Flows in conjunction with open boundary conditions represents a promising strategy for improving ergodicity in the sampling of topology within lattice gauge theories, paving the way for more efficient and accurate future simulations.

title: Jianmu-Q: Bridging Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Hardware with AI Agents
comment: 13 pages, 9 figures, 4 tables. Code available at https://github.com/Jianmu-lab/Jianmu-Q
summary: Quantum computing offers a promising approach to non-perturbative simulations of quantum field theories, particularly for real-time dynamics and systems affected by the sign problem. Yet translating continuum field theories into quantum computations remains a challenging interdisciplinary task. Here we introduce \texttt{Jianmu-Q}, a multi-agent framework that transforms natural-language descriptions of quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows. Specialized agents handle theoretical formulation, lattice discretization, qubit mapping, and circuit design, while physical consistency checks and independent numerical calculations provide validation throughout the workflow. We benchmark the framework on three field theories of increasing complexity: the $(1+1)$-dimensional Nambu--Jona-Lasinio and Schwinger models, and a $(2+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory. Across these systems, noiseless quantum-circuit simulations converge toward independent exact-diagonalization and tensor-network results, while selected circuits are executed on IBM quantum hardware, demonstrating an end-to-end, validation-guided approach to quantum simulation of field theories.

AI.tldr: A multi-agent framework, Jianmu-Q, is introduced to transform natural-language descriptions of quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows. It was benchmarked on three field theories and showed convergence with independent methods, with some circuits run on IBM quantum hardware.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to address the challenge of translating continuum field theories into quantum computations, which is a crucial step in using quantum computing for non-perturbative simulations of quantum field theories, especially for real-time dynamics and systems with a sign problem.
AI.method: The method involves the development of a multi-agent framework called Jianmu-Q, which takes natural language descriptions of quantum field theories and converts them into quantum simulation workflows. This process includes theoretical formulation, lattice discretization, qubit mapping, and circuit design, with validation through physical consistency checks and numerical calculations.
AI.result: Jianmu-Q was tested on three field theories of increasing complexity, showing that noiseless quantum-circuit simulations converge towards results from exact-diagonalization and tensor-network methods. Additionally, certain circuits were successfully executed on IBM quantum hardware.
AI.conclusion: The conclusion is that the Jianmu-Q framework provides an end-to-end, validation-guided approach for simulating field theories on quantum computers, demonstrating its effectiveness across different models and its potential for practical applications in quantum field theory simulations.

title: The hadronic-vacuum-polarization contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in isospin-symmetric lattice QCD with twisted-mass fermions
summary: We present a lattice-QCD calculation of the leading-order hadronic-vacuum-polarization (HVP) contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in isospin-symmetric QCD. We employ the gauge configurations generated by the Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration (ETMC) with $N_f = 2 + 1 + 1$ flavors of Wilson-clover twisted-mass quarks at four lattice spacings and at values of the quark-mass parameters matching the definition of isospin-symmetric QCD given in the FLAG review 2024 and in the 2025 edition of the Muon $g-2$ Theory Initiative White Paper (WP25). After retuning the simulation parameters to precisely match these two definitions of isospin-symmetric QCD, and after carrying out an extrapolation to the continuum limit based on the data at lattice spacings $a \simeq 0.049, 0.057, 0.068$ and $0.079$~fm, and spatial lattice sizes up to $L \simeq 7.7$~fm, we obtain $a_μ^{\rm HVP, FLAG}(\rm{iso}) = (720.0 \pm 6.9) \times 10^{-10}$ and $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso}) = (714.8 \pm 7.4) \times 10^{-10}$. Our results, which have a relative uncertainty of about $1 \%$, agree well with the corresponding determinations by other lattice groups. After adding to our determination of $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso})$ the leading isospin-breaking corrections provided in the WP25, namely $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}({\rm IB}) = 0.1(3.4)\times 10^{-10}$, we obtain for the full HVP the value $a_μ^{\rm HVP}= (714.9 \pm 8.1)\times 10^{-10}$. This result translates into a Standard Model prediction for the muon anomalous magnetic moment that is fully consistent with the latest result by the Fermilab Muon $g-2$ experiment and strengthens the tension between lattice QCD and data-driven (pre-CMD3) dispersive determinations.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a lattice-QCD calculation of the leading-order hadronic-vacuum-polarization (HVP) contribution to the muon's anomalous magnetic moment in isospin-symmetric QCD, with results that support the Standard Model prediction and align with recent experimental findings, while highlighting discrepancies with some other theoretical approaches.
AI.motivation: The motivation behind this research is to provide an accurate lattice-QCD calculation of the HVP contribution to the muon's anomalous magnetic moment, which is crucial for testing the Standard Model. The work aims to reduce uncertainties and resolve tensions between different theoretical and experimental determinations of this value.
AI.method: The researchers used gauge configurations from the Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration (ETMC) with 2+1+1 flavors of Wilson-clover twisted-mass quarks, across four lattice spacings, and matched quark-mass parameters to definitions of isospin-symmetric QCD. They performed a continuum limit extrapolation and included isospin-breaking corrections to refine their calculations.
AI.result: The study resulted in two precise values for the HVP contribution to the muon's anomalous magnetic moment under different definitions of isospin-symmetric QCD: $a_μ^{\rm HVP, FLAG}(\rm{iso}) = (720.0 \pm 6.9) \times 10^{-10}$ and $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso}) = (714.8 \pm 7.4) \times 10^{-10}$. Including isospin-breaking corrections, the full HVP contribution was determined to be $a_μ^{\rm HVP}= (714.9 \pm 8.1)\times 10^{-10}$, consistent with the latest Fermilab Muon $g-2$ experiment result.
AI.conclusion: The conclusion of the paper is that the calculated HVP contribution to the muon's anomalous magnetic moment supports the Standard Model prediction and is in agreement with the most recent experimental data from the Fermilab Muon $g-2$ experiment. It also highlights a discrepancy with pre-CMD3 dispersive determinations, contributing to the ongoing discussion about potential new physics.
